copy_rules: Write natural business Japanese in です/ます form, as a Japanese B2B marketer would write it from scratch. No casual forms, no katakana-heavy translationese, no literal English slogans.
Headlines speak to the buyer as a complete phrase or a question about their situation. Never a label that lists topics or names a source, like 「国内比較記事とBtoB向け設計」.
On-screen points are short noun phrases ending in a noun (体言止め), at most 20 characters, no trailing 。.
Write the product name in Latin letters on screen and in headlines; in narration write its katakana reading so the voice pronounces it correctly.
Lead with the buyer's concern (risk, security review, operational burden) and concrete proof before the product claim.
Prefer specific numbers, certifications and named customers or sources over superlatives. Never use 最高, 最強, No.1 or 革命的 unless a source says it.
Never mention that something comes from an article or research (no 記事によると, 調査では) in headlines or narration; source names belong in on-screen source chips.
Keep each narration line under 45 Japanese characters so it reads in about 5 seconds. One sentence per scene, ending in 。.
Prefer low-commitment calls to action such as 資料請求 or 無料で試す; close with a polite request form (〜ください).
style_rules: Higher information density than a US page: headline plus two or three short supporting points per scene, each with a small source chip.
Show proof on screen: source names, numbers, certifications, customer or partner names and logos when sourced.
Use the brand's own colors; set Japanese text in Noto Sans JP, weight 700 for headlines, 500 for body, line-height 1.5 or more.
Headline 64 to 80px, supporting points 32 to 40px; never break a Japanese word across lines, keep generous margins.
Calm, precise motion: fades and short slides of 300 to 500ms, staggered reveals. No slang, no bouncing or exaggerated effects.
Keep the logo visible in a corner on every scene and end on the logo, call-to-action button and URL.

questions.q: Is the tone appropriate for a Japanese enterprise buyer?
Are security, data location or support concerns addressed with evidence?
Is there local proof such as Japanese customers, partners, pricing in yen or local sources?
Is it clear what the product does and what to do next?
